cases.title: HAMMERLING
cases.line: A fifteen-second ad for a merge game: three openings to test, one tower to build, every placement cut from one master.
cases.role: Concept, art direction, AI generation, animation, sound, all formats
cases.brief: Mobile games buy their players with short ads, and the first two seconds decide whether anyone stays. A merge game needs an opening that stops the thumb and a body that shows the game feels good to play.
cases.idea: A small blacksmith builds a tower floor by floor. Merge three ingots into a sword, three swords into a legend, and the tower grows with every merge. Three openings, one about failure, one about satisfaction, one about the character, run into the same film, so a test measures only the hook.

lab.title: Switch *the hook*
lab.line: The first two seconds are the only thing that changes. Pick an opening and the ad starts over; from second two on, all three are the same film.
lab.why: Testing hooks on the same body tells you what stops the scroll, because nothing else in the ad changes.

craft.title: Three ways to *stop the thumb*
craft.text: Failure, satisfaction, character: three openings that test three different reasons to stay. Each makes its promise in under two seconds, then hands over to the same gameplay.

craft.title: Every placement *from one master*
craft.text: 9:16 for Stories, Reels and TikTok, 4:5 and 1:1 for feeds, 16:9 for YouTube and in-app. Each format is laid out again, not cropped, so the line and the button always sit in the safe area.

craft.title: Gameplay you can *read in a second*
craft.text: Big pieces, one merge per beat, a floor for every merge, then the whole tower lights up gold before the button. The end card asks once: Play free.

cases.result: Three hooks in four formats, fifteen seconds each, ready to run against each other on every placement.

hero.label: Hook C · “Help me finish the tower.” · 9:16

cases.problem_short: The first two seconds of a game ad decide whether anyone stays, so the opening has to be tested, not guessed.

cases.title: LANTERNFIN
cases.line: A fifteen-second ad for an arcade fishing game: three openings to test, one dive to the bottom, every placement cut from one master.
cases.role: Concept, art direction, AI video, animation, sound, all formats
cases.brief: An arcade fishing game lives on one pull: the deeper you go, the rarer the catch. The ad has to sell that feeling in fifteen seconds, and the first two have to stop the scroll.
cases.idea: An otter captain lowers a glowing lure into the abyss. The depth counter jumps zone by zone, every zone gives a rarer fish, and a legendary lantern-fish waits at the bottom. Three openings, failure, satisfaction and character, run into the same dive.

lab.title: Switch *the hook*
lab.line: The first two seconds are the only thing that changes. Pick an opening and the dive starts over; from second two on, all three are the same film.
lab.why: Testing hooks on the same body tells you what stops the scroll, because nothing else in the ad changes.

hooks.text: I lost my lantern down there. Help me?

craft.title: Three ways to *stop the thumb*
craft.text: A line that snaps, a fish out of the dark, an otter asking for help: three openings that test three different reasons to stay, then hand over to the same dive.

craft.title: Every placement *from one master*
craft.text: 9:16 for Stories, Reels and TikTok, 4:5 and 1:1 for feeds, 16:9 for YouTube and in-app. Each format is laid out again, so the otter, the counter and the button never fight for the same spot.

craft.title: Generated life, *animated game*
craft.text: The living shots, the otter, the boat and the fish of the abyss, are generated video. The counter, the rare cards, the type and the button are animated on top, so the game stays sharp and readable.

cases.result: Three hooks in four formats, fifteen seconds each, ready to run against each other on every placement.

cases.title: Live on the Streets
cases.kicker: Billboards · DOOH · Campaigns · ITS · ITHS · FSU
cases.line: 50+ billboards across Belgrade, designed for the three seconds a driver gives them.
cases.brief: Three schools in one group, all chasing the attention of teenagers and parents in a loud city. A driver gives a billboard three seconds, and a new campaign was due almost every month.
cases.idea: Treat every billboard like the first three seconds of a reel: one message, one image, one move. Make the end frame strong enough to print, and ship every board with its social, web and email set.

lab.title: Drive *past it*
lab.line: Most people meet a billboard at speed, at night, for a few seconds. Pick a speed and a school, drive by, then see what a driver takes home.
lab.why: Design for the glance, not the desk. A message that survives 130 km/h survives a feed.

craft.title: A new board, *every month*
craft.text: Each month the group booked the same boards across Belgrade and changed the message: pre-enrolment, a new course, a spring intake, a programme for career changers. The red and the two crests stay, so a driver knows the school before reading a word. Every board went to print in 8×3, 4×3 and 5×2.6 metres, with a LED animation and a social set.

cases.title: Baby Boo
cases.line: Product films and stills without a studio, and a cast of hand-drawn friends from the labels that comes to life.
cases.client: Baby Boo · natural cosmetics, made by moms
cases.role: Concept, art direction, generation, character animation, edit, finishing
cases.brief: Premium films and stills for a small natural-cosmetics brand. No studio, no crew, no shoot day, and the jar has to look exactly like the one on the shelf.
cases.idea: Direct it like a commercial shoot: the label stays true to the real product, the honey pours on cue, the bees sit in shallow focus. And the friends drawn on the labels get a life of their own: one ink line, cut into parts, so every one of them can move.

lab.title: Wake the *cast*
lab.line: Every jar has a friend on its label, drawn by hand in one ink line and cut into parts so it can move. Tap one to wake it, or run bath time for all five.
lab.why: A mascot that moves works everywhere: a sticker, a loading screen, the next film. Drawn once, it keeps paying back.

craft.title: Product-true, *frame by frame*
craft.text: Label, mascot, cap and proportions stay true to the real jar in every frame, so the stills can sell the product, not just a mood.

craft.title: One bold idea *per still*
craft.text: Break the glass in case of a sudden voyage. A claw machine full of jars. A carousel of giraffes. Each launch got one idea strong enough to post on its own.

rows.label: Break glass in case of a sudden voyage

craft.title: Cut like a *commercial*
craft.text: Vertical first, timed to the beat, graded as one spot: the pilot runs as a 9:16 for Reels and TikTok with a 4K master for the web.

cases.result: Vertical-first product films for Reels and TikTok, a 4K master for the web and a library of concept stills for every launch.

cases.title: Ballies
cases.kicker: Character design · NFT collection · Brand universe
cases.line: A team of characters built to be collected, then cast in three years of launches, seasons and key art.
cases.role: Digital artist · characters, NFT art direction, campaigns, motion
cases.brief: A sports prediction app needed a face. Not one mascot, a whole roster: characters fans could own, trade and play with, strong enough to front every launch for years.
cases.idea: Draw one player, perfectly. Lock the pose, proportions and line on a single rig, and let personality live in traits: headwear, eyes, arms, balls and kits. One body, 9,999 characters.

lab.title: Mix a *Ballie*
lab.line: Every Ballie is ten layers drawn on one rig, so any trait fits any other. Spin for a new one, tap a part to swap it, lock what you like.
lab.why: A character system buys variety that never breaks the brand: billions of collectible faces that still read as one team.

craft.title: One rig, a roster of *personalities*
craft.text: Pose, proportions and line weight never change, so every trait swaps cleanly and the set reads as one team. Personality lives in the details: a wink, a jester hat, a robot arm, a planet for a ball.

craft.title: The cast goes *to work*
craft.text: The characters front everything: holiday drops, tournaments, AI features, the roadmap. A cast people recognise turned a daily posting schedule into one ongoing story.

cases.title: APSIS
cases.line: Live betting apps move the odds under your thumb, show the win before the risk and hide the limits. APSIS fixes all three inside the bet flow.
cases.disclaimer: Concept project — not a real product. No real-money gambling. Teams, players and odds are fictional; demo credits only.
meta: UX research, flows, UI design, design system, live prototype
Odds jump under the thumb, the win is loud and the risk is small, and the limits sit four screens deep.
A working prototype of the whole bet flow on desktop, tablet and phone, every exception state included.

hero.label: APSIS on a wide screen: a live match with the bet slip open

problem.who: People who bet on live matches from a phone: one hand, short bursts, attention split with the game.
problem.today: Odds refresh while the thumb is on its way, so the tap lands on a price nobody read. The slip shows the possible win in big type and the stake in small. Limits and breaks live four screens deep in settings, far from the money.
problem.goal: A bet in three taps that never lands at an unseen price, with the risk as loud as the win and the limits one tap from the balance.
problem.measures_note: Targets for a usability test, not results
measures: from odds to a placed single
bets placed at odds the user did not see
contrast on every number, on every screen

research.note: No interviews or usability tests were run for this concept. What follows is a heuristic review against Nielsen's ten heuristics, of patterns that live-betting interfaces commonly use, plus one assumption of my own. Each insight says which it is.

insights.title: The odds jump under the thumb
insights.text: Live prices refresh several times a minute and cells reflow when markets open or close. A tap meant for 1.85 can land on 1.67, or on the next market.

insights.tag: Heuristic review · match with the real world
insights.title: The win is loud, the risk is small
insights.text: Possible returns get the biggest type on the slip; the stake, the amount you can actually lose, is a grey label beside the input.

insights.title: Limits are four screens deep
insights.text: Deposit and time limits sit under Account, Settings, Responsible gambling, so the tools exist but are not where the decision is made.

insights.title: Neon costs legibility
insights.text: A futuristic look tends to put glow and gradients behind the numbers. I assume the odds have to win that fight on every screen, and kept the effects away from them.

personas.note: Proto-personas: assumptions to test, not research findings

items.name: The live-match regular
items.job: When the game turns, I want to back what I just saw in seconds, so I don't miss the price.
items.needs: Stable targets, one-handed reach, a slip that never covers the score.

items.name: The weekend multi builder
items.job: When I plan Saturday, I want to stack picks and see the total odds and stake clearly, so I know what I'm risking.
items.needs: Readable totals on a phone, easy removal, Singles beside Multi.

items.name: The careful one
items.job: When I set a budget, I want the app to hold me to it without lectures, so betting stays fun.
items.needs: The limit visible near the money, plain words, a break that is easy to take.

flow.title: Three taps, every exception in words
flow.text: From odds to a placed bet is three taps: odds, stake, place. Everything that can go wrong is checked before the last tap counts, and every exception has one way out that never places a bet by itself.

ia.title: The slip is one tap away, everywhere
ia.text: Five places, no deeper than two levels. The bet slip is not a page but a layer every screen can open, and Limits hangs off the balance, not off Settings.

screens.title: Odds that *stay* put
screens.text: The first screen is the live list. Every match has the same three cells in the same place, so the eye and the thumb learn one target.
why: Fixed 1 / X / 2 cells: a price change only changes colour and an arrow, never the layout.
The empty slip teaches the flow in one line: “Pick, stake, place: three taps.”
The balance sits inside a ring that fills as today's limit is used.
A “Concept · demo credits only” pill stays on screen, so a screenshot can't pass for a real product.

screens.title: The risk as *loud* as the win
screens.text: The slip opens beside the scoreboard on desktop and as a sheet on a phone, so the game never disappears behind it.
why: “You can lose” sits above Returns, at the same size.
Quick stakes +5 / +10 / +25 / +50 for one thumb, no keyboard needed.
A limit bar shows the bet against today: “38.00 of 100.00 used · 58.00 after this bet”.
The button names the amount, so the last tap reads as a sentence.

screens.title: Limits beside the *money*
screens.text: Limits open with one tap on the balance from anywhere, and read as today's ring, not as a settings form.
why: Lowering a limit applies at once; raising one takes 24 hours.
Reality check every 15, 30 or 60 minutes: time, staked and net, in plain numbers.
Take a break for 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days, two taps away.
This session's net is always shown, win or loss, without colour drama.

system.text: Every colour, face and radius is named once, as a token. The odds button is the main component, and its states carry the whole live behaviour.
system.motion: A price change is colour plus an arrow, never movement. With reduced motion the flash is off and the arrows stay.

responsible.text: Responsible play is not a page here, it is the exceptions of the bet flow. Each one stops the bet, says what happened in plain words and offers one way out.

items.title: Odds changed
items.text: The price moved before the tap counted: the new odds in amber, and nothing is placed until you accept them.

items.title: Market suspended
items.text: The button goes dim and says why. You can wait or remove the pick.

items.title: Over today's limit
items.text: It shows what is left and offers to set the stake to exactly that.

items.title: Reality check
items.text: At your interval: time, staked and net. Take a break is as big as Keep going.

items.title: Limits
items.text: Today as a ring, the daily limit, reality check and breaks on one screen.

items.title: My bets
items.text: Open and settled bets show stake and returns side by side.

test.text: Five people who bet on sport at least monthly, 20 minutes each, remote, thinking aloud, on the live prototype with demo credits.
